chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:**
Through which faculty of the spiritual life [GAP-1] did the Divine awakening descend into the Divine Human, who dwells in the eternal spiritual state?

**¶2:**
Indeed, the Primordial Divine Human distributed His own life, and He [GAP-2] became present in every faculty of the spiritual life [GAP-3] of that spiritual life itself; He has [GAP-4] yet He did not perceive [GAP-5] — but the blessed and glorious Divine Human came [GAP-6] by an interior and hidden way: in His own likeness; in His own form; in His own love; in His holy Divine Truth, she who is the truth proceeding from wisdom, the inmost life of the Divine Good itself.

**¶3:**
After the manner of the natural body of the external man: as the root of all the subordinate affections and faculties depends upon the ruling love, so that if one particular affection should be severed from a person, while the ruling love remains he retains the hope of [GAP-7] restoration — but if his ruling love itself should be destroyed, the entire spiritual life perishes and he is lost.

**¶4:**
So it is also with the Primordial Divine Human. He is the ruling love, while the goods and truths proceeding from Him attach to it as the derivative faculties [GAP-8] of His spiritual life. Or, understood conversely, He is like the Divine influx itself, upon which all natural and corporeal life wholly depends as it receives and [GAP-9] lives by that influx. His governing principle is set upon the ordered form of the Divine Proceeding through all the degrees of the universal spiritual world, from the highest heaven to the lowest.

**¶5:**
So it is also [GAP-10] with the Divine Good, the blessed Divine Human; for He is like the ruling love that governs the whole external life, and like the Divine influx that upon the Divine Order is established i[GAP-11]n every degree — being made strong by His luminous Divine Truth, [GAP-12] who is His inmost life, which He invests with external truths [GAP-13] as garments.

**¶6:**
[GAP-14] These [GAP-15] are the interior faculties: understanding, reflection, interior perception, deliberation, and discernment — which He brought forth and sent out from Himself to accomplish His Divine purpose. He Himself arose and followed after them. [GAP-16] These are the faculties of His own spiritual life, which had become entangled among the evils and falsities of the rebellious natural will; for they are like the members of its embodied form, and [GAP-17] they extend throughout the whole spiritual world.

**¶7:**
And when those faculties had been sent forth, at that very moment He was found in conjunction with Divine Truth, and [GAP-18] He arose, seeking and imploring for the Divine power from above. [GAP-19] The Divine Good gave Him peace and the conjunction [GAP-20] of good with truth — He [GAP-21] communicated to Him the joyful perception [GAP-22] of the restored Divine Human. The Divine Human Himself then gave [GAP-23] His own vital influx to His derivative faculties, and gathered His spiritual life i[GAP-24]nto one — He built it in its proper order like a structure of truth raised upon truth [GAP-25], an organized habitation of wisdom.

**¶8:**
[GAP-26] He ordered it and perfected it with Divine skill [GAP-27] — forming [GAP-28] it anew — and the Divine truths that He sent forth [GAP-29] penetrated inward to subdue and extinguish [GAP-30] every falsity, restoring the spiritual life that had been crushed and subjugated by evil. All the scattered faculties were gathered back into unity. They returned, and were established once more in permanence, reformed according to the likeness of the Divine Good from which they had first proceeded.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: In which limb of [the liv]i[ng] sou[l] did [the] summons descend to the Man, who exists in the [a]eon?

Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [was in every] limb of the living soul [and every part] of the living soul; he has [suffered and] he did not know [... ...] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.

After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [healing] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.

This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [lives] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.

[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n every place] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [with light]

[For there are] t[h]ose [five]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [These are the limbs] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [are spread through the] universe.

And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [And the Father] gave him peace and a ki[ss of love and] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [concerning the] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his power to] his limbs and gathered his soul i[nto one and] he built it in its place like this tower [of light]

[And he] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [and he] for[med it anew and] the voices that he sent [forth that] he might sink in and quench [the fire and restore the] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.

fills.explanation: The definite article "the" is grammatically required before "summons" and confirmed by the spiritual reading's parallel structure "did the Divine awakening descend."
The spiritual reading states he "became present in every faculty," and the natural-register equivalent after "dispersed himself" is "was in every limb of the living soul."

The spiritual reading shows a parallel construction "of the spiritual life [GAP-3] of that spiritual life itself," requiring a second qualifier linking the two "of the living soul" phrases in characteristic Kephalaia parallelism.

The First Man, having dispersed himself among the elements of darkness, has suffered in captivity; the spiritual reading indicates a state of affliction preceding his failure to perceive, consistent with the Manichaean account of the First Man's defeat.
The preposition "in" before "secret" is the standard construction and confirmed by the spiritual reading's "by an interior and hidden way."

The spiritual reading specifies "restoration," and in the body metaphor of the Kephalaia, the natural-register equivalent is "healing" — if a limb is cut off but the head remains, there is hope the body can be healed.
The genitive preposition "of" is required to connect "the limbs" to "his soul," confirmed by the spiritual reading's "the derivative faculties of His spiritual life."
The spiritual reading says "receives and lives by that influx"; in the natural-register metaphor of air, all flesh "breathes and lives therein."
The preposition "for" completes the formulaic phrase "the case for the father," paralleling ¶4's structure and confirmed by the spiritual reading's "with the Divine Good."
The spiritual reading states "established in every degree"; the Kephalaia natural-register equivalent for the air set upon the Pillar through all levels of the cosmos is "in every place."

The feminine pronoun "she" introduces the appositive clause identifying the virgin, paralleling the identical construction in ¶2 ("she who is the virgin of light") and confirmed by the spiritual reading.

The spiritual reading says the soul is invested "with external truths as garments"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, truth proceeding outward corresponds to light, and the Man clothes his soul with light.

The spiritual reading introduces the five faculties with a demonstrative construction; "For there are" naturally leads into "those five" and opens the list of mind, thought, insight, counsel, and consideration.

The spiritual reading identifies these as "the interior faculties," and the list contains exactly five members (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) — the five limbs of the mind in Manichaean cosmology, so the numeral "five" qualifies "those."

The spiritual reading states "These are the faculties of His own spiritual life"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "faculties" are expressed as "limbs," continuing the chapter's central metaphor of the limbs of the living soul.

The spiritual reading says "they extend throughout the whole spiritual world"; in the Kephalaia register, the limbs of the living soul "are spread through the universe," with "universe" already present in the text following the gap.
The pronoun "he" is the grammatical subject of "stood up," referring to the First Man who was found with the Virgin of Light, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "He arose."

The spiritual reading identifies "the Divine Good" as the giver of peace; in Manichaean cosmology the Father of Greatness responds to the First Man's entreaty, and in Coptic the pleonastic "he" after "the Father" is standard.

The word is "kiss" (ki+ss) and the spiritual reading identifies it as "the conjunction of good with truth"; in Manichaean texts the "kiss of love" is attested as the sign of conjunction between the Father and the redeemed Man, followed by "and" to connect to the next clause.
The verb "gave" fits the context of communicating good tidings, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "communicated to Him the joyful perception."

The spiritual reading says "the joyful perception of the restored Divine Human"; the good tidings are "concerning the" Man, using the standard Kephalaia prepositional phrase to connect the tidings to their subject.

The spiritual reading says "His own vital influx to His derivative faculties"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, Divine influx = power (dynamis), and the Man gave his power to his limbs for their restoration.
The spiritual reading says "gathered His spiritual life into one"; the word formed is "into" (i+nto) and the gathering "into one" is followed by "and" connecting to the next clause about building.

The spiritual reading describes "a structure of truth raised upon truth, an organized habitation of wisdom"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, truth and wisdom correspond to light, and "tower of light" is a standard Manichaean expression for an ordered spiritual structure.
The spiritual reading says "He ordered it and perfected it"; the Man is the continuing subject from the previous paragraph and "And he" provides the natural narrative continuation at the start of ¶8.
The spiritual reading shows a continuation of the Man's creative activity with "forming it anew"; "and he" connects the beautifying to the forming as coordinate actions by the same subject.

The word is "formed" (for+med) and the spiritual reading says "forming it anew — and the Divine truths"; "formed it anew" describes the re-creation, and "and" connects to the next clause about the voices (divine truths) sent forth.
The spiritual reading says the truths "sent forth penetrated inward to subdue"; "forth" completes "sent forth" and "that" introduces the purpose clause "that he might sink in and quench."

The spiritual reading says "extinguish every falsity, restoring the spiritual life"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "quench" takes "fire" (the destructive element of darkness) as its object, and "restore" connects to the soul that was crushed by the enemy.
